title: IBS Case Study Digest Volume-II
outcomes: Use portfolio and value chain analysis on a case.
Apply related party, revenue and audit requirements.

meta.exam_tip: In merger questions, always comment on EPS effect and synergies, not just the ratio.

concepts.title: Portfolio and value chain analysis
body: The BCG matrix places businesses by market growth and relative market share: stars (high growth, high share), cash cows (low growth, high share), question marks (high growth, low share) and dogs (low growth, low share). Cash from cows funds stars and selected question marks.

Porter's value chain splits a firm into primary activities (inbound logistics, operations, outbound logistics, marketing and sales, service) and support activities (infrastructure, HR, technology, procurement). Advantage comes from performing activities at lower cost or in a way that creates differentiation.
Combining the two shows where to invest and which activities to strengthen, outsource or integrate.
concepts.analogy: Know where cash comes from and where value is made.
concepts.work: A mature biscuit brand with leading share is a cash cow.

concepts.title: Strategic cost management
body: Target costing starts from the market price, deducts the required margin and treats the result as the maximum allowable cost; the gap to current cost is closed through value engineering before launch.

Life-cycle costing tracks costs from design to withdrawal; activity-based costing traces overheads to products by drivers, exposing loss-making SKUs; Kaizen supports continuous small improvements after launch.
Pricing strategies — penetration, skimming, premium — must align with the competitive strategy (cost leadership or differentiation).
concepts.work: A ₹8 per pack gap on 25 lakh packs means ₹2 crore of savings to find.

concepts.title: Acquisitions and risk management
body: Acquisitions are tested on strategic fit, valuation and post-merger effects. Swap ratios may use EPS, market price, book value or intrinsic value; paying a higher P/E than the acquirer's dilutes EPS unless synergies add earnings.
Due diligence covers financial, tax, legal and operational areas; integration risk often decides success.

Risk management uses forwards, futures, options and swaps to hedge currency, commodity and interest exposures; the hedge decision compares the locked-in cost with the expected unhedged cost and the company's risk appetite.
concepts.analogy: Deals must create value after integration.
concepts.work: Booking a forward at ₹84.20 for an import payable removes the risk of the rupee weakening.

concepts.title: Governance, reporting and related parties
body: Section 188 of the Companies Act covers contracts with related parties (sale or purchase of goods, leasing, services, agency, appointment to office). They need board approval, and shareholders' approval by ordinary resolution where prescribed limits are crossed; interested members cannot vote. Transactions in the ordinary course of business at arm's length are outside these approvals.

Ind AS 24 requires disclosure of related party relationships and transactions; Ind AS 115 treats trade discounts, rebates and price concessions as variable consideration, estimated and constrained, reducing revenue.
Auditors assess related party risks (SA 550) and may report significant matters as key audit matters for listed entities (SA 701).
concepts.analogy: Related party deals need approvals, disclosure and audit focus.
concepts.work: Buying packaging from a director's firm above market price needs scrutiny.

illustrations.title: Target costing for a new snack line
illustrations.q: Hearthstone Foods Ltd. plans a millet snack. Market research fixes the price at ₹120 per pack, and the company wants a 25% margin on price. The current engineered cost is ₹98 per pack and volume is 25 lakh packs a year. Compute the target cost, cost gap and the annual saving needed, and suggest how to close the gap.

solution.text: Close the gap through value engineering (lighter packaging, fewer SKUs), supplier collaboration on millet sourcing, and process redesign; launch only when the gap is closed or the price strategy changes.

checks.label: Target cost: target price less 25% margin (₹ per pack)
Cost gap: current cost less target cost (₹ per pack)
Annual saving needed on 25 lakh packs (₹)

illustrations.title: Share exchange for Rasoi Spices
illustrations.q: Hearthstone (2 crore shares, earnings ₹60 crore, price ₹400) acquires Rasoi Spices (50 lakh shares, earnings ₹9 crore, price ₹120) through a share swap based on market prices. Compute the swap ratio, shares issued and post-merger EPS assuming no synergy. Compare with Hearthstone's pre-merger EPS.

solution.text: EPS rises from ₹30 to about ₹32.09 even without synergy, because Rasoi is bought at a P/E of 6.67 (₹120 ÷ ₹18 EPS) against Hearthstone's own 13.33. EPS accretion alone does not prove value creation; the board should still test strategic fit, synergies and integration risk.

checks.label: Swap ratio on market prices: target price ÷ acquirer price
New Hearthstone shares issued for 50 lakh target shares
Post-merger EPS: combined earnings ÷ total shares (₹)

jobs.title: Acquisition screening memo
jobs.situation: The board wants a view on acquiring a regional spice brand.
steps: Assess strategic fit and BCG position.
Compute swap ratio and EPS effect.
jobs.takeaway: EPS dilution is acceptable only with credible synergies.

mcqs.q: A business with low market growth and high relative share is a:
Procurement in Porter's value chain is a:
Paying a higher P/E for the target than the acquirer's own P/E, without synergy, tends to:
mcqs.explain: Merger arithmetic. In practice: synergies needed.

mcqs.q: A forward contract for an import payable protects against:
mcqs.explain: Locks the rate. In practice: forgoes upside.

mcqs.q: Related party transactions in the ordinary course at arm's length under section 188:
options: Need no board or shareholder approval under the section
mcqs.explain: Third proviso. In practice: document arm's length.

mcqs.q: Volume rebates to distributors are treated under Ind AS 115 as:
mcqs.explain: Estimate and constrain. In practice: accrue rebates.

summary: BCG: stars, cash cows, question marks, dogs.
Value chain: primary and support activities.
Swap ratio and EPS dilution; synergies decide.
Section 188 approvals; Ind AS 115 variable consideration; SA 550.
remember: Arm's length ordinary-course deals are outside section 188 approvals.
traps: Treating above-market supplies from a relative as arm's length.

viva.q: How should cash cows be managed?
viva.model: Hold position efficiently and use their surplus cash to fund stars and selected question marks.
Redesigning a product or process to cut cost while keeping the functions customers value.

viva.q: What does due diligence cover in an acquisition?
viva.model: Financial, tax, legal and operational review of the target to find risks and validate value.

viva.q: Can an interested shareholder vote on a related party resolution?
viva.model: A related party member must abstain from voting on that resolution under section 188.

viva.q: Which standard governs audit of related parties?
viva.model: SA 550 requires the auditor to identify and assess related party risks.

cases.title: Hearthstone Foods — integrated case
cases.case: Hearthstone Foods Ltd. sells biscuits (market leader, category growth 3%), ready meals (growth 18%, share 4%) and frozen desserts (growth 2%, share 3%). It imports oat flakes worth US$5 lakh payable in 3 months; the 3-month forward rate is ₹84.20 and treasury expects spot of ₹84.80. It buys cartons from Pack Prime LLP, where the managing director's brother is a partner, at prices 12% above market.

mcqs.q: Ready meals in the BCG matrix are a:
mcqs.explain: High growth, low share. In practice: invest or exit.

mcqs.q: Expected saving from booking the forward (₹ lakh):
The carton purchases from Pack Prime are:
options: Related party transactions needing section 188 approvals
Exempt as ordinary course at arm's length
mcqs.explain: Above market, so not arm's length. In practice: board approval.

mcqs.q: Frozen desserts fall in which quadrant?
mcqs.explain: Low growth, low share. In practice: harvest or divest.
